caption:
Anthropic says its own AI did a job that used to take dozens of engineers 6 to 12 months.
Its Mythos model got Claude running on AMD's MI355X chips in about three days, with almost no human help, and wrote or ported nearly all the low-level GPU code.
The claim comes from Anthropic's IPO investor presentation and has not been independently verified.

Is Nvidia's software moat starting to crack?

paragraphs.text: Anthropic says its Mythos model got Claude running on AMD's MI355X graphics processors in about three days, with almost no human intervention. The company made the claim in the investor presentation for its initial public offering, The Decoder reported on November 11, 2026. OfficeChai reported the same figures from Anthropic's roadshow material on the same day.

According to Anthropic, bringing a large model up on a new chip family has traditionally taken six to 12 months of work by dozens of engineers. Anthropic worked with AMD GPUs for the first time this year.

Every chip family needs its own low-level software, known as kernels, plus a tailored inference stack, OfficeChai noted. Anthropic says Mythos ported or wrote nearly 100 percent of the kernels needed for the AMD bring-up. The Decoder points out that the notes on Anthropic's chart refer to prompt processing of an Anthropic model on MI355X GPUs, while the text speaks of Claude, so the exact model tested is not fully specified.

Neither publication was able to verify the figures independently. They come from Anthropic's own disclosures. OfficeChai also reported that AMD chief executive Lisa Su has said the extra engineering support AMD had planned to provide was not needed, though it did not publish a direct quote.

Tom Brown, Anthropic's co-founder and chief compute officer, says the company now trains and runs Claude on all four major chip families, according to The Decoder. He described the early choice to spread work across vendors as an unconventional bet and said years of investment had made the company very good at porting. Anthropic treats compute from different vendors, architectures and locations as a single pool.

OfficeChai lists Nvidia GPUs, Amazon's Trainium chips and Google's TPUs in that pool alongside AMD. Anthropic's relationship with Google includes a deal for up to a million TPUs, and the company also has an in-house chip design team as part of its long-term plans.

Anthropic also described what it calls compute multipliers, research advances that get more performance out of the same hardware, and a program called Anthropic Direct, in which it leases chips and runs them in purpose-built data centers to lower the total cost of ownership.

AMD agreed in July 2026 to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic as deployment milestones are met. Anthropic plans to deploy up to two gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs in Helios rack-scale systems, with the first gigawatt phase starting in the first half of 2027, The Decoder reported. Nvidia committed to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic in November 2025, and Anthropic's amended SEC registration statement of November 10, 2026 lists Nvidia among seven technology companies in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price.

For years, the software built around Nvidia's CUDA platform has made it costly for AI labs to move work to other chips. If a model can now do most of that porting in days, the cost of switching drops, and buyers gain leverage over chip suppliers. The claim is also part of an IPO pitch, which gives Anthropic a reason to present its efficiency in the best light, so independent results will matter.
Watch whether AMD or outside engineers confirm the three-day figure, and whether other labs report similar AI-driven chip bring-ups once the AMD Helios systems start arriving in 2027.
